source_checks.requirement: TaskStore::write_task_state uses write_file_atomically instead of raw fs::write plus fs::rename.
write_file_atomically creates a sibling temporary file with create_new, writes and fsyncs the file, renames it into place, and fails closed if the Unix parent directory sync fails.
RunLedger::append_many fsyncs appended terminal evidence and syncs the run directory before terminal transition markers are removed.
McpStdioDeadline carries a process-local monotonic expiration instant and reconstructs remaining timeout budget instead of resetting the budget between stdio response wait and child-exit wait.
stdio_request waits for the MCP child to exit only until the remaining McpStdioDeadline and then records process-tree kill evidence on timeout.
MCP stdio subprocesses run in their own Unix process group, timeout handling terminates the process tree, and timeout errors expose bounded process-tree cleanup evidence.
Runtime tests cover MCP stdio timeout cleanup and approval timeout terminalization without approval reuse.

Task terminal status updates acquire a per-run terminal-mutation lock, re-read latest state inside the lock, and require expected current status plus updated_at freshness before terminal completion or cancellation evidence.
Terminal status transitions persist terminal-transition.json before state mutation, append a prebuilt terminal ledger event, and recover a state-written/ledger-missing process-loss window on restart.
Test-only durable write failpoints cover disk_full_before_write, truncated_state_before_rename, and rename_denied_after_sync without replacing committed state or leaking temporary files.

Unix process-group cleanup remains the enforced local process-tree implementation; Windows process-tree termination, stale-lock recovery, atomic-replace durability, directory durability, reparse point handling, macOS CI, Windows CI, and Runtime-wide persisted deadlines remain required-before-release gaps.

closure.implemented_scope: Unix/local MCP stdio monotonic deadline accounting, process-tree cleanup evidence, durable write failure injection, and crash-consistent terminal task state/ledger transition recovery.
closure.summary: RRP-7.1 no longer claims broad platform/deadline/durability closure. It closes the local Unix MCP stdio deadline and terminal mutation corrective slice by sharing one process-local monotonic MCP stdio deadline across response and child-exit waits, killing late-exit Unix process trees with bounded evidence, serializing terminal task mutations under a per-run lock, persisting terminal-transition markers before terminal state writes, recovering missing terminal ledger evidence after process loss, and proving durable-write fail-closed behavior under deterministic disk-full, rename-denial, and truncated-temp failpoints.

remaining_required_before_release: Runtime-wide persisted wall-clock task/run deadline propagation and resume-time expiry checks
Windows stale migration and terminal mutation lock recovery
Windows atomic replace and directory durability semantics
junction/reparse point and symlink/path canonicalization hardening
non_goals: hosted scheduler, daemon, worker fleet, and generic shell execution remain out of scope
direct GitHub workflow hardening remains in runtime-release-guard-ci
semantic protocol/event contract generation remains in RRP-5.1
license, publish, tag, release, and release asset decisions remain owner-controlled
runtime_release_ready remains false until the CI blocker, protocol semantic contract blocker, and owner decisions close
